questions.stem: Translate the following into English: 你好！我叫小红。我很好，谢谢。
markscheme: B1: correct translation of 你好！我叫小红。— 'Hello! My name is Xiaohong / I am called Xiaohong'
B1: correct translation of 我很好，谢谢。— 'I am (very) well, thank you'
questions.modelAnswer: 你好！我叫小红。= 'Hello! My name is Xiaohong.' — 我叫 … is the self-introduction pattern 'I am called …'. 我很好，谢谢。= 'I am very well, thank you.' — 很 links the subject to the adjective (it does not have to mean 'very' strongly), and this is the standard reply to 你好吗？

questions.stem: Complete each sentence with the correct word from the box: 岁 · 月 · 点 · 分 (two words are not needed). (a) 我今年十二＿＿。(I am twelve years old this year.) (b) 现在三＿＿半。(It is now half past three.)
markscheme: B1: (a) 岁 — age is stated with the pattern number + 岁
B1: (b) 点 — clock times use number + 点, with 半 for half past
questions.modelAnswer: (a) 我今年十二岁。— age takes the pattern number + 岁, with no 是. (b) 现在三点半。— the hour is number + 点, and 半 adds 'half past', so 三点半 = 3:30. The distractors do not fit: 月 means month and 分 means minutes.

questions.stem: Translate the following into English: 我家有四个人。我家有一只猫。
markscheme: B1: 'There are four people in my family' (我家有四个人)
B1: 'My family has a cat / there is a cat in my family' (我家有一只猫)
questions.modelAnswer: 我家有四个人 = 'There are four people in my family' — people are counted with the measure word 个. 我家有一只猫 = 'My family has a cat' — most animals take the measure word 只. The verb 有 means 'to have' and also 'there is / there are'.

questions.stem: Translate the following into Chinese, using simplified characters: (a) I like eating dumplings. (b) My grandpa loves drinking tea. (c) I would like a cup of tea.
markscheme: B1: (a) 我喜欢吃饺子。— 喜欢 followed directly by the verb 吃
B1: (b) 我爷爷爱喝茶。— correct verb 喝 for a drink
B1: (c) 我想喝一杯茶。— 想 for 'would like' plus the drink measure word 杯
questions.modelAnswer: (a) 我喜欢吃饺子。(Wǒ xǐhuan chī jiǎozi.) — 喜欢 can be followed directly by another verb: 喜欢吃 = like eating. (b) 我爷爷爱喝茶。(Wǒ yéye ài hē chá.) — tea is drunk, so the verb must be 喝, never 吃. (c) 我想喝一杯茶。(Wǒ xiǎng hē yì bēi chá.) — 想 is the polite 'would like', and drinks are counted with the measure word 杯.

questions.stem:
Read the passage and answer the questions in English.

今天天气很好，是晴天，二十五度。明天会下雨，有一点儿冷。我最喜欢秋天，因为天气不冷也不热，很凉快。

(a) What is the weather like today? (b) What will the weather be like tomorrow? (c) Why does the writer like autumn best?
markscheme: B1: (a) it is a sunny / fine day, twenty-five degrees (是晴天，二十五度)
B1: (b) it will rain and turn a little cold (明天会下雨，有一点儿冷)
B1: (c) because in autumn it is neither cold nor hot — pleasantly cool (不冷也不热，很凉快)
questions.modelAnswer: (a) Today the weather is very good: it is a sunny day and the temperature is twenty-five degrees. (b) Tomorrow it will rain and be a little cold — 会 marks a future forecast here, not 'can'. (c) The writer likes autumn best because the weather is neither cold nor hot but pleasantly cool; the reason is introduced by 因为.

questions.stem: Translate the following into English: 我们上午有四节课。数学比英语难。
markscheme: B1: 'We have four lessons in the morning' (我们上午有四节课)
B1: 'Maths is harder than English' — 比 correctly understood as 'than'
questions.modelAnswer: 我们上午有四节课 = 'We have four lessons in the morning' — lessons are counted with 节, and the time word 上午 comes before the verb. 数学比英语难 = 'Maths is harder than English' — the pattern A 比 B + adjective means A is more (adjective) than B; 很 is never added after 比.

questions.stem: Write 3–5 sentences in Chinese describing your home. You must include: how many rooms your home has; one piece of furniture and where it is; and one adjective that describes your home or a room.
markscheme: B1: states the number of rooms with a correct pattern, e.g. 我家有三间房间 / 我家有四个房间
B1: names a furniture item and locates it correctly with 在, e.g. 沙发在电视前面 / 书在桌子上
B1: uses a suitable adjective correctly with 很, e.g. 我的房间很干净 / 我的家很大
questions.modelAnswer: Example answer: 我家有三间房间：一个客厅、一个厨房和一个卧室。客厅里有一个沙发。沙发在电视前面。我的家不大，但是很干净。我很喜欢我的家。(My home has three rooms: a living room, a kitchen and a bedroom. There is a sofa in the living room. The sofa is in front of the TV. My home is not big, but it is very clean. I really like my home.) Rooms are counted with the measure word 间, location is expressed with 在, and adjectives follow 很 without 是.

questions.stem:
Translate the following mini-dialogue into Chinese, using simplified characters.
A: How much is this pair of trousers?
B: Three hundred yuan.
A: Too expensive! Can it be a bit cheaper?
markscheme: B1: 这条裤子多少钱？— measure word 条 for trousers plus 多少钱
B1: 三百块。— price as number + 块, with no verb needed
B1: 太贵了！能便宜一点儿吗？— the 太…了 pattern and a polite 能…吗 request
questions.modelAnswer: A: 这条裤子多少钱？(Zhè tiáo kùzi duōshao qián?) — trousers take the measure word 条. B: 三百块。(Sānbǎi kuài.) — a price needs no verb: just number + 块. A: 太贵了！能便宜一点儿吗？(Tài guì le! Néng piányi yìdiǎnr ma?) — 太…了 means 'too …', and 能 + verb + 吗 forms a polite request, literally 'can it be a little cheaper?'
